name: Washington motorcycle knowledge tests (2-wheel)
description: Questions from the Washington DOL Motorcycle Operator Manual for the two-wheel motorcycle knowledge tests. A 2-wheel endorsement takes four tests at a DOL partner training school: the permit knowledge test (50 multiple-choice questions, pass with 80%) and permit skills test, then the endorsement knowledge test (25 questions, pass with 68%) and endorsement skills test. DOL does not publish its test questions, so these are written from the manual.

source.name: Washington State Department of Licensing, Motorcycle Operator Manual

questions.prompt: What do you need to ride a motorcycle legally on Washington roads?
answers: A motorcycle instruction permit or endorsement
wrong: A regular driver license and motorcycle insurance
A safety course certificate and a helmet
A motorcycle registration in your own name
questions.explanation: A permit or endorsement is required on public roads, on top of your driver license.

questions.prompt: What can happen to your motorcycle if you ride it on public roads without the required permit or endorsement?
answers: It may be impounded
questions.explanation: Riding without a permit or endorsement can get the motorcycle impounded, and the minimum fine is $389.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum fine for riding without a motorcycle endorsement?
questions.explanation: The manual gives $389 as the current minimum fine.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum age for a motorcycle instruction permit?
questions.explanation: You must be at least 16 and hold a current Washington driver license.

questions.prompt: Who may ride as a passenger with a motorcycle instruction permit holder?
answers: Nobody, permit holders may not carry passengers
wrong: Only a rider with a full endorsement
questions.explanation: A permit allows no passengers and no riding at night.

questions.prompt: When may a motorcycle instruction permit holder ride?
answers: Only in daylight, not at night
wrong: Only with an endorsed rider following
questions.explanation: Permit holders may not ride at night or carry passengers.

questions.prompt: How long is a motorcycle instruction permit valid?
answers: 180 days
questions.explanation: A permit lasts 180 days and can be renewed once before it expires.

questions.prompt: How many times can you renew a motorcycle instruction permit?
answers: Once, before it expires
questions.explanation: You can renew once before it expires; if it lapses, you retest for a second permit. You may hold only 2 permits in 5 years.

questions.prompt: How many motorcycle instruction permits may you hold within 5 years?
questions.explanation: Only 2 permits in a 5-year period.

questions.prompt: What must riders under 18 do before applying for a motorcycle endorsement?
answers: Complete an approved safety course, with a parent’s permission
wrong: Hold a permit for a full year with no tickets
Ride with an endorsed adult for 50 hours
Pass the skills test twice in a row
questions.explanation: Under-18 riders need an approved safety course and parental permission for the course and the endorsement.

questions.prompt: Do you have to take a training course to take the motorcycle permit or endorsement tests (if you are 18 or older)?
answers: No, training is not required
questions.explanation: Training is optional for adults, though the tests are taken at a DOL partner training school.

questions.prompt: Where do you take Washington motorcycle permit and endorsement tests?
answers: At a DOL partner training school
questions.explanation: All the tests are given through DOL partner training schools.

questions.prompt: After passing the required tests, how long must you wait before adding the endorsement at a licensing office?
answers: 3 business days
questions.explanation: There is a 3-business-day wait. Passing results are good for 180 days.

questions.prompt: Do 2-wheel and 3-wheel motorcycles need separate endorsements in Washington?
answers: Yes, each has its own tests and endorsement
wrong: No, one endorsement covers every motorcycle
Only for sidecar rigs, not trikes
Only if the engine is over 150 cc
questions.explanation: A 2-wheel and a 3-wheel endorsement are separate.

questions.prompt: Is liability insurance required for motorcycles in Washington?
answers: Yes, it is mandatory
questions.explanation: Liability insurance is mandatory for all motorcycles (RCW 46.30.020).

questions.prompt: When may motorcycles use HOV (diamond) lanes in Washington?
answers: At any time
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may use HOV lanes at any time.

questions.prompt: Is lane splitting (riding between lanes of traffic) legal in Washington?
answers: No, it is against the law
questions.explanation: Riding between lanes and riding on the shoulder are both illegal.

questions.prompt: Is riding on the shoulder to get past traffic legal in Washington?
answers: No, it is against the law
questions.explanation: Shoulder riding and lane splitting are both illegal.

questions.prompt: Can two motorcycles legally ride side by side in one lane in Washington?
answers: Yes, but it leaves no room to maneuver
wrong: Only in a group of three or more
questions.explanation: It is legal, but the manual advises caution because it limits space and escape paths.

questions.prompt: What kind of helmet does Washington law require on a motorcycle?
answers: A DOT-compliant helmet
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet is the legal minimum. Snell and ECE are optional extras.

questions.prompt: Where do you find the label showing a helmet meets the DOT standard?
answers: On the back of the outside and on the inside
wrong: On the chin strap buckle only
Only on the box it came in
On the visor and the front of the shell
questions.explanation: DOT labels are on the helmet’s rear exterior and its interior.

questions.prompt: May you wear a novelty helmet on public roads?
answers: No, they are not DOT-compliant
wrong: Yes, any helmet meets the law
questions.explanation: Novelty helmets do not meet the DOT standard and are not legal on 2- or 3-wheel motorcycles.

questions.prompt: When does Washington law require eye protection?
answers: Whenever the motorcycle has no windshield
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required unless the motorcycle has a windshield.

questions.prompt: Are in-ear speakers (earbuds) legal while riding in Washington?
answers: No, earbuds are not legal
questions.explanation: Earplugs for hearing protection are legal; earbuds with speakers are not.

questions.prompt: Are earplugs for hearing protection legal while riding in Washington?
answers: Yes
questions.explanation: In-ear hearing protection is legal; in-ear speakers are not.

questions.prompt: Which type of helmet gives the most protection?
answers: Full-face
questions.explanation: A full-face helmet protects the chin and face too. Half and 3/4 shells do not.

questions.prompt: What does a 3/4 or half shell helmet not protect in a crash?
answers: Your chin and face
questions.explanation: Only full-face (and modular) helmets cover the chin and face.

questions.prompt: What is the inner liner of a DOT helmet usually made of?
answers: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam
questions.explanation: A DOT helmet has a hard outer shell, an impact-absorbing EPS liner, comfort padding and a retention strap.

questions.prompt: When should you replace a helmet?
answers: After a crash, or if it is cracked or its straps are frayed
wrong: Only when it no longer fits your head
Every year, whether or not it is damaged
Never, as long as it still looks fine
questions.explanation: Replace it after any crash or defect; many makers also recommend replacing it every 5 years.

questions.prompt: How often do many manufacturers recommend replacing a helmet?
answers: Every 5 years
questions.explanation: Even without a crash, many makers say every 5 years.

questions.prompt: How should a helmet fit?
answers: Snug all the way around, without moving or causing pain
wrong: Loose enough to move so air can circulate
Tight enough that it leaves a headache
Tipped back so it does not block your view
questions.explanation: It should not move or lift off while riding, cause pain, or block your vision or hearing.

questions.prompt: What gives the most protection for your eyes and face?
answers: A helmet with a shatter-resistant face shield
wrong: A tall windshield on its own
questions.explanation: Glasses are usually not shatter-resistant and can blow off; a windshield does not fully protect either.

questions.prompt: Why are ordinary eyeglasses or sunglasses not enough eye protection?
answers: Most are not shatter-resistant and can blow off at speed
wrong: They are too dark for most daylight riding
Washington law bans them while riding
They fog up quickly in the sun and heat
questions.explanation: Use goggles or a face shield instead.

questions.prompt: When should you not wear tinted eye protection?
answers: In low light, such as dusk, fog or rain
questions.explanation: Tints cut what little light there is.

questions.prompt: Which of these is something a face shield should do?
answers: Let air through to reduce fogging
questions.explanation: It should be scratch-free, penetration-resistant, give a clear view ahead and to the sides, fasten securely, vent, and leave room for glasses.

questions.prompt: Which material gives the best protection in a jacket or pants?
answers: Leather or sturdy abrasion-resistant material
questions.explanation: Denim does not give significant abrasion protection.

questions.prompt: Where should riding gear have body armor?
answers: Knees, elbows, shoulders, hips and back
wrong: Only the chest and the stomach
Only the wrists and the ankles
Only the neck and the head
questions.explanation: Armor inserts at the impact points.

questions.prompt: What kind of boots should you ride in?
answers: Sturdy boots that cover your ankles
wrong: Low shoes that leave the ankles free
questions.explanation: They should be reinforced at the ankle, shin, toe and heel, with laces tucked in.

questions.prompt: Why should you tuck in your boot laces?
answers: So they do not catch on the motorcycle
wrong: So they stay dry in the rain
questions.explanation: Loose laces can catch on pegs and controls.

questions.prompt: Which gear colors help other drivers see you?
answers: Bright or light colors, with retroreflective strips
wrong: Black, so you look like a serious rider
Dark blue or gray, so you match traffic
questions.explanation: If you like black gear, wear a high-visibility reflective vest over it.

questions.prompt: Why should you wear hearing protection, even with a full-face helmet?
answers: Wind and road noise can permanently damage your hearing
wrong: Washington law requires it on freeways
So you cannot hear sirens and horns
So you can play music over the noise
questions.explanation: Pick protection that cuts harmful noise but still lets you hear horns and sirens.

questions.prompt: Why dress in layers?
answers: So you can add or remove them as the weather changes
wrong: To look bigger to other drivers
To pad yourself instead of armor
questions.explanation: Cold brings fatigue and hypothermia; heat brings sunstroke and dehydration.

questions.prompt: What is the legal minimum protective gear in Washington?
answers: A DOT helmet, and eye protection without a windshield
wrong: A helmet only, and nothing else
A helmet, a jacket and gloves
Nothing at all for riders over 18
questions.explanation: The manual says to wear the most protective gear possible at all times.

questions.prompt: In the T-CLOCS pre-ride inspection, what does the T stand for?
answers: Tires and wheels
questions.explanation: Check air pressure, tread, sidewalls, wheels and spokes.

questions.prompt: In the T-CLOCS pre-ride inspection, what does the O stand for?
answers: Oil and other fluids
questions.explanation: Check levels and look for leaks.

questions.prompt: In the T-CLOCS pre-ride inspection, what does the first L stand for?
answers: Levers and controls
questions.explanation: Levers, pedals, cables, hoses and the throttle. The second L is Lights.

questions.prompt: In the T-CLOCS pre-ride inspection, what does the second L stand for?
answers: Lights
questions.explanation: Headlight, taillight and brake lights, turn signals and switches.

questions.prompt: In the T-CLOCS pre-ride inspection, what does the first S stand for?
answers: Suspension and drivetrain
questions.explanation: Suspension, and the chain, belt or drive shaft. The last S is Stands.

questions.prompt: In the T-CLOCS pre-ride inspection, what does the last S stand for?
answers: Stands
questions.explanation: The kickstand, and the center stand if there is one.

questions.prompt: When checking tires before a ride, what do you look at?
answers: Air pressure, tread, and sidewall or wheel damage
questions.explanation: Also look for loose spokes.

questions.prompt: Which of these is part of checking the Lights in T-CLOCS?
answers: Turn signals and switches
questions.explanation: Headlight, tail and brake lights, turn signals and switches.

questions.prompt: Where should you keep your knees while riding?
answers: Against the gas tank
questions.explanation: It helps balance and control in turns, accelerating and braking.

questions.prompt: How far forward should you sit?
answers: So your arms are slightly bent on the handgrips
wrong: So your arms are straight and locked
As far back on the seat as you can
So your chest rests on the gas tank
questions.explanation: Steer with your arms; do not hold yourself up with them.

questions.prompt: How should you hold your right wrist on the throttle at the start?
answers: Flat
questions.explanation: A flat wrist keeps you from rolling on too much throttle by accident.

questions.prompt: Where should your hands be compared with your elbows?
answers: Even with or below your elbows
questions.explanation: Adjust the handlebars to fit.

questions.prompt: Where should you keep your feet while riding?
answers: Firmly on the footrests
wrong: Dragging on the ground for balance
questions.explanation: Never drag them; keep them where you can reach the pedals.

questions.prompt: Which brake gives the most stopping power?
answers: The front brake
questions.explanation: Weight shifts forward when you slow down.

questions.prompt: What gives the shortest, safest stop?
answers: Using both brakes smoothly and progressively
wrong: Using only the rear brake, firmly
Using only the front brake, hard
questions.explanation: Without skidding either tire.

questions.prompt: Why should you never grab the front brake?
answers: You could skid or go over the handlebars
wrong: It wears the brake pads out quickly
It can stall or shut off the engine
It is against the law in Washington
questions.explanation: Squeeze it smoothly and progressively.

questions.prompt: Above about what speed does a motorcycle have to lean to turn?
answers: 12 to 15 mph
questions.explanation: Below that you can turn the bars without much lean.

questions.prompt: To turn left, which way do you press the handlebars?
answers: Press the left grip
questions.explanation: Pressing the left grip makes the bike lean and turn left. This is countersteering.

questions.prompt: What is countersteering?
answers: Pressing the grip toward your turn to start the lean
wrong: Turning the bars the opposite way in a skid
Steering by pushing with your feet
Turning the bars hard toward the turn
questions.explanation: Press left, go left; press right, go right.

questions.prompt: What are the four steps of cornering on a motorcycle?
answers: Slow, look, press, roll
questions.explanation: Slow before the corner, look through it, press to lean, roll on the throttle.

questions.prompt: When should you slow down for a curve?
answers: Before you enter it
questions.explanation: Set your entry speed first so you do not need to brake while leaned over.

questions.prompt: Where should you look in a corner?
answers: Through the turn, toward the exit
wrong: At the road just ahead of your tire
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.prompt: What should you do with the throttle after entering a corner?
answers: Roll on gently to keep or slightly increase speed
wrong: Close it completely and coast through
Twist it wide open to power out
Pull in the clutch and coast through
questions.explanation: A little throttle steadies the motorcycle.

questions.prompt: You are going wide in a curve. What should you do?
answers: Press harder on the inside grip
wrong: Look at the edge of the road
questions.explanation: More countersteering pressure tightens your line.

questions.prompt: Why does braking in a curve take extra care?
answers: Leaning leaves less traction for braking
wrong: The brakes are weaker when hot
It does not, braking is the same
questions.explanation: The more you lean, the less traction is left.

questions.prompt: You must stop while in a curve. What should you do?
answers: Straighten the motorcycle first, then brake
wrong: Use only the front brake while leaned
questions.explanation: If you cannot straighten first, brake gently and add pressure as the bike straightens. Square the bars before you stop.

questions.prompt: Which cornering line is generally safest for less experienced riders?
answers: Middle, middle, middle
questions.explanation: It keeps you away from oncoming traffic and edge gravel, though oil can collect in the center.

questions.prompt: How do you make a quick stop?
answers: Use both brakes fully without locking either wheel
wrong: Lock the rear wheel and skid to a stop
Use only the rear brake as hard as you can
Brake hard while swerving around it
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front harder as it loads; keep your knees on the tank to stay straight.

questions.prompt: What is a swerve?
answers: Two quick countersteers, around the hazard and back
wrong: One hard stop with both brakes
Leaning your body off the seat
Riding onto the shoulder to stop
questions.explanation: Keep your body upright and let the bike move under you.

questions.prompt: Should you brake and swerve at the same time?
answers: No, swerve then brake, or brake then swerve
wrong: Yes, but only with the rear brake
questions.explanation: Each needs all your traction.

questions.prompt: Why would you swerve instead of stopping quickly?
answers: When there is no room to stop, or traffic behind cannot
wrong: Swerving is always better than braking
Stopping quickly is illegal on freeways
Swerving keeps your speed up in traffic
questions.explanation: Practice both at different speeds.

questions.prompt: What is the downside of slowing with engine braking (downshifting)?
answers: Your brake light does not come on
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light a few times.

questions.prompt: What does a wet clutch help you with?
answers: Smooth starts and control at low speed
questions.explanation: The clutch controls the power going to the rear wheel.

questions.prompt: Which kind of motorcycle should a new rider start on?
answers: A smaller, lighter one
wrong: The most powerful one they can afford
questions.explanation: Sit on it to check you can reach all the controls and get on and off easily.

questions.prompt: How far ahead should you look while riding?
answers: At least 12 seconds
wrong: Just past the vehicle in front
questions.explanation: Looking well ahead gives you time to spot hazards and plan.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended minimum following distance in ideal conditions?
answers: 3 seconds
questions.explanation: 3 seconds is the minimum for 2- and 3-wheelers; add more for bad weather, poor surfaces, traffic, fatigue and night.

questions.prompt: When should you increase your following distance?
answers: In bad weather, heavy traffic, at night or when tired
wrong: Only when a car is tailgating you
questions.explanation: 3 seconds is the minimum in ideal conditions.

questions.prompt: What are the three parts of total stopping distance?
answers: Perception, reaction and execution
questions.explanation: At 60 mph (90 feet a second) a rider covers about 360 feet seeing, reacting to and stopping for a deer.

questions.prompt: At 60 mph, how far do you travel each second?
answers: About 90 feet
questions.explanation: That is why it takes about 360 feet to perceive, react and stop.

questions.prompt: Where do most collisions between motorcycles and other vehicles happen?
answers: At intersections
questions.explanation: The most common is a car turning left across the motorcycle’s path.

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of motorcycle-car crash?
answers: A car turning left in front of the motorcycle
wrong: A car rear-ending a stopped motorcycle
A car changing lanes into the motorcycle
A car backing out of a driveway
questions.explanation: It happens at intersections. If a car is waiting at a green light, expect it to turn.

questions.prompt: A car is waiting to turn at a green light as you approach. What should you expect?
answers: That it may turn across your path
wrong: That it will wait for you
Nothing, you have the right of way
questions.explanation: Cover your controls, look for an escape path and make sure it has stopped before you go.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to “cover” your controls?
answers: Keep your fingers and foot ready on the brake and clutch
wrong: Keep the brakes lightly on all the time
Put a weatherproof cover over the grips
Hold the throttle steady in one spot
questions.explanation: Covering the controls cuts your reaction time at intersections and hazards.

questions.prompt: What gear should you stay in when stopped at an intersection?
answers: First gear
questions.explanation: So you can move away quickly if a vehicle behind you does not stop. Check your mirrors often.

questions.prompt: Someone is tailgating you. What should you do?
answers: Gradually slow down to make more space ahead
wrong: Speed up to get away from them
Brake hard to warn them off
Wave them past onto the shoulder
questions.explanation: Speeding up can trap you between two vehicles.

questions.prompt: Before changing lanes, what should you do besides checking your mirrors?
answers: Look over your shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot
wrong: Sound your horn to warn other drivers
Flash your headlight at the car ahead
Speed up so you can merge faster
questions.explanation: Mirrors do not show your blind spots.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in passing another vehicle?
answers: Move to the left side of your lane to see farther ahead
wrong: Close up right behind it to get a run
Sound your horn so the driver knows
Move onto the shoulder to see ahead
questions.explanation: Then check it is not turning and you are in a passing zone, signal, check your blind spot, change lanes, and cancel the signal.

questions.prompt: What is one advantage of riding in the left part of your lane?
answers: You can see around the vehicle ahead and be seen in its mirror
wrong: It keeps you far from oncoming traffic and wind blast
It is the part of the lane with the most traction
Washington law requires motorcycles to ride there
questions.explanation: The trade-off is being closer to oncoming traffic and its wind blast.

questions.prompt: How many lane positions does each traffic lane have?
answers: Three: outside, middle and inside
questions.explanation: Your position changes with each new hazard or change in traffic.

questions.prompt: When using engine braking to slow down, what should you do so drivers behind you know?
answers: Flash your brake light a few times
wrong: Nothing, the brake light comes on by itself
questions.explanation: Engine braking does not turn on the brake light.

questions.prompt: Which of these makes you more visible to other drivers?
answers: Bright gear, extra lights and a good lane position
wrong: Riding in a vehicle’s blind spot
Dark gear and a tinted visor
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where you can be seen, and move out of blind spots.

questions.prompt: How should you change your riding at night?
answers: Slow down and increase your following distance
wrong: Ride faster to spend less time on the road
Follow closer to use their lights
Use only your high beam and keep the same speed
questions.explanation: Use every light source, including the vehicle ahead’s headlights and brake lights, and the fog line.

questions.prompt: When are animals most active on the road?
answers: Between dusk and dawn
questions.explanation: Watch for wildlife, especially in corners.

questions.prompt: What is target fixation?
answers: Staring at a hazard so you steer toward it
wrong: Aiming for the apex of a curve
Focusing on the car ahead to follow it
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go, not at the hazard.

questions.prompt: What do time and space give you in traffic?
answers: Time to plan for a hazard, and room to act
wrong: A faster trip through heavy traffic
Better fuel economy on the highway
The right of way at intersections
questions.explanation: Always know where your escape path is.

questions.prompt: Which of these surfaces is slippery for a motorcycle?
answers: Painted lines and manhole covers
questions.explanation: Also leaves, oil spots, drainage grates and gravel.

questions.prompt: Where in a lane do oil drips and leaves tend to collect?
answers: Near the middle
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars down the center of the lane.

questions.prompt: When are roads especially slippery?
answers: After the first rain of the season
wrong: After a long dry spell, before it rains
questions.explanation: Oil that built up while it was dry comes to the surface.

questions.prompt: When should you change speed or direction around a slippery surface?
answers: Before you reach it, not on it
questions.explanation: Over the slippery patch, handle the controls gently and keep your eyes up.

questions.prompt: At what angle should you cross railroad tracks or a speed bump?
answers: As close to 90 degrees as you can
questions.explanation: A shallow angle can catch your tire.

questions.prompt: How should you ride over an obstacle you cannot avoid?
answers: Rise slightly off the seat, eyes up, a bit of throttle
wrong: Sit down hard and brake on top of it
Look down at it and coast across
Swerve around it at the last moment
questions.explanation: Your legs absorb the shock and your weight goes onto the footpegs; roll off as the tire crosses.

questions.prompt: Where should you look when riding over a slippery patch or obstacle?
answers: Ahead, up the road
questions.explanation: You go where you look.

questions.prompt: How old must a motorcycle passenger be?
answers: At least 5 years old
questions.explanation: They also need a passenger seat, footrests and a DOT-compliant helmet.

questions.prompt: What equipment does a motorcycle passenger need?
answers: A seat, footrests and a DOT helmet
wrong: A backrest and a seat belt
questions.explanation: And they must be at least 5 years old.

questions.prompt: Where should a passenger keep their feet?
answers: On the footrests at all times
questions.explanation: Even when the motorcycle is stopped.

questions.prompt: When should you adjust your mirrors when carrying a passenger?
answers: After the passenger is seated
questions.explanation: The extra weight changes the bike’s angle.

questions.prompt: How should you load cargo?
answers: Strapped down, centered and as low as possible
wrong: Stacked high on the rear rack
All on one side, in a saddlebag
In a bag hung from the handlebars
questions.explanation: It must not get in the way of the controls. Check the owner’s manual for weight limits.

questions.prompt: Where do you find your motorcycle’s maximum load?
answers: In the owner’s manual
questions.explanation: Passengers and cargo change how it accelerates, stops and handles.

questions.prompt: What formation should a group usually ride in?
answers: Staggered
questions.explanation: Switch to single file in curves, where you cannot see far, or where you need more time and space.

questions.prompt: When should a group switch to single file?
answers: In curves, where visibility is limited, or where more space is needed
wrong: At every stop sign and signal
questions.explanation: Single file in right-hand curves keeps the outside riders off the centerline.

questions.prompt: What following distance should you keep behind the rider ahead in a group?
answers: At least 3 seconds
questions.explanation: The same minimum as riding alone.

questions.prompt: Who should wait before riding in a group?
answers: Newer riders, until they have experience
wrong: Nobody, groups are safest for new riders
questions.explanation: Group rides bring peer pressure to ride beyond your skill.

questions.prompt: When does alcohol start to affect your riding?
answers: With the first drink
questions.explanation: It affects judgment, vision, attention and fine motor skills.

questions.prompt: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) counts as intoxicated for riders 21 and over?
questions.explanation: Riders under 21 have a lower limit of 0.02%.

questions.prompt: What is the BAC limit for riders under 21?
questions.explanation: Adults 21 and over are intoxicated at 0.08%.

questions.prompt: On average, how long does your body take to get rid of one drink?
answers: About one hour
questions.explanation: More drinks in an hour take longer still.

questions.prompt: Which of these lowers your blood alcohol level?
answers: Only time
questions.explanation: Nothing else removes alcohol from the body.

questions.prompt: Which of these is one standard drink?
answers: A 12 oz. beer
questions.explanation: One drink is a 12 oz. beer, a 5 oz. glass of wine or 1½ oz. of hard alcohol.

questions.prompt: How much wine is one standard drink?
answers: 5 oz.
questions.explanation: Same as a 12 oz. beer or 1½ oz. of hard alcohol.

questions.prompt: How much hard alcohol is one standard drink?
answers: 1½ oz.
questions.explanation: Same as a 12 oz. beer or a 5 oz. glass of wine.

questions.prompt: Can over-the-counter medicines such as cold or allergy remedies affect your riding?
answers: Yes, some impair you as much as alcohol
questions.explanation: Combined with even one drink, their effect is much stronger.

questions.prompt: For adults 21 and over, what blood THC level counts as impaired?
answers: 5 nanograms
questions.explanation: Marijuana slows reactions and distorts your sense of time and distance.

questions.prompt: What happens if you refuse a breath test?
answers: Your license is suspended
wrong: You must retake the knowledge test
questions.explanation: Suspension is mandatory for a DUI conviction, an arrest, or refusing a breath test.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to avoid riding impaired?
answers: Choose to drink or to ride, not both
wrong: Wait 15 minutes after your last drink
questions.explanation: Plan other transportation for yourself or an impaired friend.

questions.prompt: Besides alcohol and drugs, what can impair your riding?
answers: Fatigue, strong emotions and distractions
wrong: Riding with a full tank of fuel
Using both brakes at every stop
questions.explanation: Ask yourself before every ride whether you are tired, upset, distracted, or have had a drink or medicine.

questions.prompt: Your friends want you to keep up with them on a fast group ride. What should you do?
answers: Ride at your own skill level
wrong: Keep up so the group stays together
questions.explanation: Resist peer pressure; talk about experience and comfort before the ride.

tests.name: Permit knowledge test
tests.why: Like the 2-wheel permit knowledge test: 50 multiple-choice questions, and you pass with 40 right (no more than 10 wrong).

tests.name: Endorsement knowledge test
tests.why: Like the 2-wheel endorsement knowledge test: 25 multiple-choice questions, and you pass with 17 right (no more than 8 wrong).

tests.name: Riding skills and strategy
tests.why: Drill the riding sections of the manual, weakest questions first, with the answer after each one.
